spot.html_text: The probability of our perceptual belief and expectations of experience isn’t simply a matter of the natural or objective frequency with which such beliefs are true or expectations fulfilled, or of their propensity for such, in the face of the sensory data and memories that stimulate them. Lewis rejects frequency and propensity understandings of probability (advocated by Peirce and others) for a version of the logical theory of probability. Probability is a logical relation between a conclusion

Strict implication is an intensional notion, and the logic of strict implication is a form of modal logic.
